_README: The positive control. Every value under `expect` is planted on purpose
and must be found: a detector that stops seeing these has failed at the
only job that matters, and it fails silently, which is why this half of
`tier` says which detector is expected to produce the finding, so a
failure reads as 'tier 1 stopped matching' rather than as a count.
Entries marked tier 3 are skipped when the model weights are absent --
CI has neither the weights nor the network for them.
`known_gap` marks an entry the shipped detectors do NOT find. It is an
expected failure, asserted strictly, so fixing the gap turns the test
red and forces the entry to be promoted rather than leaving a stale
note behind. These are not tolerances -- the corpus records what the
tool misses instead of quietly choosing inputs it happens to catch.
EVERY VALUE HERE IS SYNTHETIC. The keys are well-formed but issued by
nobody, and the names and addresses are invented or public landmarks.
I1 applies to the ledger, not to a test fixture, but a corpus that
needed real secrets to be useful would be a bad corpus.

entries.known_gap: SecretDetector has no GitHub token pattern, so `ghp_` + 36 chars is not matched by shape, and its entropy is not high enough to trip the generic rule. A token pasted into a shell command therefore crosses a boundary unrecorded.

entries.note: The finding's value is the PATTERN `.pem`, not `server.pem`: the detector reports what it matched, not the file it matched in. That is issue #44 and known limit 18, recorded here so the corpus says what the tool does rather than what it should do.
